speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, chronic alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use, have you noticed any changes in the size or appearance of your right arm, such as muscle wasting or atrophy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy due to Anabolic Steroid Abuse (specifically Steroid-Induced Brachial Neuropathy or Pancoast Tumor with brachial plexus involvement).

The combination of significant weight loss, chronic alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use in a bodybuilder with progressive arm weakness and sensory loss strongly suggests a compressive neuropathy. I request images of the right shoulder and upper chest to rule out a Pancoast tumor or other compressive lesions.
